issues.description: Method mismatch for Farm.singFarmSong() and its helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal): the problem statement and the template expect singFarmSong() to print the song (void) and the template declares public void singFarmSong() and a private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) that prints lines. In the solution, singFarmSong() is implemented as public String singFarmSong() returning the full song text and the helper is private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) returning a verse. This contradicts the template and textual specification and can confuse students about whether the API should print to stdout (void) or return the song (String), leading to inconsistent implementations or failing comparisons against the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the method signatures and documented behavior consistent across all artifacts. Two viable resolutions (choose one to preserve educational intent):
1) Align to the problem/template printing intent: change the solution to declare public void singFarmSong() and private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and have them print verses using System.out.println(), and update any tests that assume a return value accordingly.
2) Align to the solution returning-text approach: update the problem statement to state that singFarmSong() returns a String containing the full song and change the template to declare public String singFarmSong() and private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (with TODOs adjusted). Ensure tests and documentation expect a returned String. 
Document the chosen approach in the problem statement and update the template and solution code so signatures match exactly.
